page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n2 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. This configuration consists of 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1399.29, categorized as weak, while the multi-core score is rated as poor at 1841.88. Memory bandwidth tests show 102.26 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 13.72 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Geekbench testing reports a single-core score of 1111.0 and a multi-core score of 1311.0. Real-world simulation benchmarks reflect these limitations, with static web serving throughput at 2.06 GB/sec and Redis SET operations executing at 1.75 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated compute resources but presents a clear tradeoff in memory density and overall throughput. With only 2.0 GB of RAM, memory-intensive workloads will face severe constraints. The instance is suited for lightweight, compute-bound tasks that do not require substantial memory footprints, such as basic text processing, simple single-threaded compilation, or low-traffic web serving.
